citations.note: Plan lists eight intent-member categories including 'required dispositions'.
PRD_MEMBER_KINDS is seven kinds; dispositions are a separate array over members.

structuralFindings.detail: The plan's eight PRD intent categories are realized as seven member kinds plus a separate dispositions array; 'required dispositions' is not an eighth member kind.

citations.note: The reconciliation fold hardcodes verdict 'consistent'.
An accepted 'gaps' verdict validates ok and still enters the chain.

structuralFindings.detail: The accepted-material fold hardcodes reconciliation verdict 'consistent' regardless of the product's actual verdict: an accepted 'gaps' report still folds as consistent, and the baseline consumes only the reconciliation revision digest.

citations.note: The desk loop iterates deskNodeIds() - the authored node-array order.
edgeTarget is a fail-closed lookup over the declared edges; no runtime router consumes the edge table.

structuralFindings.detail: The driver walks desks in authored node-array order, not by traversing FORMALIZATION_FLOW_EDGES; the edge table is installed-manifest data (plus a fail-closed edgeTarget lookup), so the runtime order guarantee is the node array order matching the edge chain.

citations.note: The driver stops at refusals (blockedAt) instead of traversing failure edges.
DRIFT_DETECTED routes to human-wait; the drift wait scenario.
freezeDriftHumanWait.

structuralFindings.detail: The failure-class edges (domain.failed x8, domain.drift-detected, domain.inconsistent) are declared but no driver step traverses them: refusals stop the run (blockedAt) and DRIFT_DETECTED routes to a typed human-input wait. The ten success+failure edges are declared; demonstrating all eighteen is owed by the plan's declared==demonstrated test layer.

citations.note: acceptedMaterialAfter has no solution-contract case; the default fold is a no-op.

structuralFindings.detail: The solution contract does not fold into AcceptedMaterial: settle-formalization is the chain terminator; its product leaves the workshop only through the Development handoff.

citations.note: validateSolutionContract pins authorities and verifies the canonical digest but never resolves the handoff binding arrays.
settleSolutionContract only requires the binding arrays non-empty.

structuralFindings.detail: validateSolutionContract is binding-blind: developmentHandoff binding arrays are never resolved against the accepted material's id sets, so foreign bindings validate ok.

citations.note: solutionContract/developmentHandoff references appear only inside the formalization workshop package (source-wide search).

structuralFindings.detail: No consumer of the Development handoff exists outside the formalization package in this tree: the Solution Contract is produced here and read by nothing (the forward derivation ends at emission).

citations.note: acceptedTraceDigest is the capsule ref; memberDigests fold the five revision digests.
The plan enumerates dispositions and evidence-method bindings as distinct baseline sections.

structuralFindings.detail: The plan's §freeze-what-baseline enumerates deferral/constraint/assumption/unknown dispositions and evidence-method bindings as distinct named baseline sections; the installed baseline folds them into memberDigests (the five revision digests) plus acceptedTraceDigest (the capsule ref).

citations.note: The imported-Discovery shell desk runs before the eight flow desks.

structuralFindings.detail: The driver runs NINE desks: the import-discovery-handoff shell desk (stage 1) plus the eight flow desks; the shell desk is outside the 11-node graph (recorded here as preFlowShellDesk).

citations.note: operatorStaffed is manifest data; the kernel sees only author/reviewer.
driveDesk resolves the same two launch kinds for every desk.

structuralFindings.detail: Kernel desks (freeze-what-baseline, settle-formalization) are operator-staffed by manifest data only; the driver staffs them identically to cells through the same author/reviewer launch kinds.

citations.note: Terminal-claim verification and lifecycle proof run after the flow settles.

structuralFindings.detail: Lifecycle terminal-claim verification (route verify-terminal-claims -> verifyTerminalClaims -> lifecycle terminal proof -> run settlement) is a post-flow ladder, not a graph node: the flow graph terminates before the lifecycle handoff.
